title: CRITICAL: PlaceObject3 HasFilterList encoded at wrong flags2 bit (0x10) — ALL 9 filters dropped by Ruffle
description:
encodePlaceObject3WithFilters (packages/swf/src/filters.ts:584) sets the HasFilterList flag as flags2 = 1<<4 (0x10). The SWF PlaceObject3 flags are a single LITTLE-ENDIAN u16 (flags1 low byte, flags2 high byte). Ruffle's swf crate (ruffle/swf/src/types.rs PlaceFlag) defines HAS_FILTER_LIST = 1<<8, which is flags2 BIT 0 (0x01) — NOT bit 4. flags2 bit 4 = overall bit 12 = HAS_IMAGE. Confirmed against Ruffle's own writer (ruffle/swf/src/write.rs write_place_object_2_or_3 writes write_u16(flags.bits()) with HAS_FILTER_LIST=1<<8).

CONSEQUENCE: every published SWF with ANY filter (all 9 types) is parsed by Ruffle's swf crate (= the runtime) as PlaceObject3 with filters=None — the entire FILTERLIST is silently ignored; Ruffle instead thinks HAS_IMAGE is set. Filters never render.

PROOF (swf crate decode, swf 0.2.2 = Ruffle runtime):
 - Real compileDocument() output (movieclip instance + ConvolutionFilter) → swf crate decodes PlaceObject3 with NO filters (both clamp/preserve cases).
 - Patching ONLY the flags2 byte from 0x10 → 0x01 makes the SAME bytes decode the ConvolutionFilter correctly: clamp=true,preserveAlpha=false → ConvolutionFilterFlags(CLAMP); clamp=false,preserveAlpha=true → ConvolutionFilterFlags(PRESERVE_ALPHA); both → CLAMP|PRESERVE_ALPHA; neither → 0x0. (This also re-proves task 1236's clamp/preserve bit-swap fix is itself correct.)

CONTROL: cacheAsBitmap uses flags2=0x04 (= crate bit 10 HAS_CACHE_AS_BITMAP) and decodes correctly, and cacheasbitmap.test.ts:262 documents 'bit 2 of flags2 = bit 10 of combined u16 PlaceFlag in Ruffle'. By that same documented mapping HasFilterList must be flags2 bit 0 (0x01), proving 0x10 is the lone misplaced bit.

FIX: filters.ts:584 change `enabledFilters.length>0 ? (1<<4) : 0` to `(1<<0)` (0x01). Also fix the comment at filters.ts:580 ('bit 4: HasFilterList' → 'bit 0: HasFilterList'). Update all byte-presence tests that assert flags2 & 0x10 for HasFilterList: blur-tween.test.ts:62-64, convolution-filter.test.ts:279-299, displacement-filter.test.ts:227-229, and any others (grep '0x10' / 'HasFilterList' under packages/swf/src/__tests__). These tests codified the wrong bit, so they currently MASK the defect (all green while filters are dropped) — same masking pattern task 1236 found for the clamp/preserve bits.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) swf crate (tools/swf-dump, swf 0.2.2) decodes filters from a real compiled SWF for all 9 filter types; (2) Ruffle e2e visual-oracle shows a filter (e.g. DropShadow/Blur) actually rendering vs an unfiltered control (byte-presence is NOT proof — see CLAUDE.md 'Byte-presence unit tests are not runtime proof'); (3) golden-parity stays exit 0.

NOTE: pre-existing defect, NOT introduced by task 1236. Discovered during QA verification of 1236 (HEAD 4e267be). Task 1236's flag-byte fix is genuine and correct but is masked by THIS bug — the corrected bits never reach Ruffle until HasFilterList is moved to flags2 bit 0.
